summary:
EcoRadar  is an interactive Earth observation platform that helps users explore and compare real NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite radar data.

The project uses NISAR Level-2 GCOV radar observations from Greenland to visualize changes between two observation dates. Users can compare satellite images side by side, explore difference maps, inspect individual pixel values, view histograms, and adjust visualization settings.

EcoRadar also provides data metadata and export options, making complex satellite observations easier to explore and understand.

Our goal is to make Earth observation data more accessible and help people investigate our changing planet through interactive satellite data visualization.

details: EcoRadar – Exploring Earth with NISAR What Does EcoRadar Do? EcoRadar is an interactive Earth observation platform that helps users explore and compare real NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite radar data. It focuses on making complex satellite observations easier to understand through interactive visualizations. Our project uses two NISAR Level-2 GCOV HHHH radar observations of Greenland, captured on October 22, 2026, and November 3, 2026. How Does It Work? EcoRadar loads real satellite radar datasets and displays them as interactive images. Users can compare two observations side by side, view a difference map, inspect individual pixel values, and explore data through histograms and visualization controls. The platform also supports linear and decibel display modes, contrast adjustments, zooming, panning, and exporting visualizations as PNG images or data as CSV files. Benefits and Intended Impact Satellite radar data can be difficult to interpret without specialized software and technical knowledge. EcoRadar provides a more accessible way to explore this information. Its intended benefits include: - Helping students and beginners understand Earth observation data. - Making real NISAR radar observations easier to explore. - Supporting educational activities and scientific exploration. - Encouraging interest in environmental monitoring and satellite technology. - Providing interactive tools for comparing and investigating radar observations. Our long-term goal is to make satellite data more accessible and encourage people to learn about changes happening on our planet. Tools and Technologies EcoRadar was developed as a web-based application using: - HTML for the application structure. - CSS for the design and responsive interface. - JavaScript for interactive features and data processing. - NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV data for real satellite observations. - ASF DAAC and NASA Earthdata Cloud for accessing the data. - GitHub for source-code hosting and version control. - GitHub Pages for website deployment. What Makes It Creative? EcoRadar combines real satellite radar data with an interactive and accessible web interface. Instead of presenting users with complicated scientific datasets alone, it provides visual comparison, difference mapping, pixel inspection, and adjustable visualization tools in one platform. It is designed to let users explore the data themselves rather than simply viewing a static satellite image. Factors We Considered During development, we considered data accessibility, visualization clarity, usability, scientific accuracy, and transparency. We included metadata to identify the source observations and clearly distinguish real satellite data from synthetic demonstration views. We also considered the scientific limitations of radar data. Differences between two HHHH observations do not independently prove glacier movement, ice loss, or environmental damage. Further scientific analysis and independent validation are necessary before making such conclusions.
